thread: rachel: Heads-up: Docusaurus linkcheck started failing on several inbound links after the mdx migration. Seems focused on headings that include inline code. docs-ci: linkcheck job failed: https://ci.internal/jobs/4999 (error: 3 broken anchors) diego: any repro? I saw a few 404s but couldn't reproduce locally. rachel: minimal repro in repo/docs/fixtures/heading-slug.md: ```md ## Using `--no-cache` flag Some text. Link: /docs/usage#using--no-cache-flag ``` When Docusaurus builds, the generated slug becomes `using-no-cache-flag` (backticks removed and multiple hyphens collapsed), but some crosslinks (autogenerated during migration) point to `using--no-cache-flag` (double hyphen). linkcheck treats them as broken. harry: I think the migration script preserved the raw code span when it converted legacy markdown links, so we ended up with mixed slug styles. The slug algorithm changed between versions (old slugify kept the literal chars instead of normalizing). diego: options: 1) update migration to rewrite links to the canonical slug; 2) add a docs-only slug-normalizer step in the build (mkdocs/docusaurus plugin) that canonicalizes both headings and inbound links; 3) convert problematic headings to explicit HTML anchors. rachel: explicit anchors work but are noisy and will confuse translators. I'd prefer a migration fix + a small sanity check in our pre-commit or docs CI to detect mismatched slugs. i18n-team-bot: note: headings with inline code are common in translated strings. any change must preserve i18n comment hints. docs-ci: opened a tracking issue: https://issues.internal/2356 - adding a link-normalizer step to the migration pipeline. harry: i'll draft a tiny script that: (a) parses headings, (b) computes the new canonical slug using the current docusaurus slugify rules, and (c) rewrites any internal links that reference the non-canonical slug. will include unit tests. diego: add an id fallback in the script too - insert a short HTML anchor after headings when an inline code span is present, e.g. `` so older links don't break while we backfill. rachel: sounds good. can we also add a docs-ci test that builds a tiny fixture site and asserts linkcheck returns zero? don't want to ship partial migrations. harry: yup PR coming with script + tests + migration runner. PR: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/930 (WIP). tagging @rachel @diego. preview-bot: Preview deploy for branch fix/slug-normalize (PR 930) succeeded: https://preview.docs.internal/930 (linkcheck green) docs-ci: migration runner applied across `content/docs` and created a migration-backup tar at gs://internal/migrations/slug-normalize-2026-03-23.tar.gz rachel: reviewed the PR, left a couple of nits about logging. once green we'll coordinate with the i18n team to avoid churn for translators. harry: addressed comments and added verbose logging behind a `--debug` flag. tests passing locally. docs-ci: CI green, linkcheck: 0 broken anchors. merging after small delay to allow any last-minute holdouts to opt-out. rachel: merging now. will update the migration guide with a short section: "Headings with inline code: slug normalization and link rewrites" and mention the id-fallback pattern for manual edits. diego: thanks all. great catch — would've been painful in prod. :relieved:
